claims: The Artemis II crew consists of NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman (commander), Victor Glover (pilot), Christina Koch (mission specialist), and CSA astronaut Jeremy Hansen (mission specialist).
The Artemis II crew successfully completed a 10-day record-setting lunar flyby mission.
The Artemis II crew splashed down in the Pacific Ocean on April 10, 2026.
Artemis II was the first crewed mission to the Moon since 1972.
Reid Wiseman is a US Navy pilot.
Reid Wiseman led the Artemis II mission.
The Artemis II mission surpassed the distance record set by Apollo 13.
Victor Glover is a Navy aviator with extensive test pilot experience.
Victor Glover became the first Black man to travel around the Moon.
Christina Koch holds the record for the longest single spaceflight by a woman (328 days).
Christina Koch became the first woman to fly around the Moon.
Jeremy Hansen is a Canadian Space Agency (CSA) astronaut.
Jeremy Hansen became the first Canadian to make a journey beyond low Earth orbit.
On April 6, 2026, the Artemis II crew traveled 252,756 miles from Earth.
The distance traveled by the Artemis II crew on April 6, 2026 surpassed the record set by Apollo 13 in 1970.
The Artemis II crew tested the Orion spacecraft's life-support systems.
The Artemis II crew conducted deep-space navigation.
The Artemis II crew observed the lunar far side.
The Artemis II crew splashed down safely near San Diego on April 10, 2026.
The Artemis II mission lasted 10 days.
The Artemis II crew captured high-resolution images of the Earth and Moon.
The Artemis II crew captured views of the far side of the Moon.
